title: Label the methodology provenance honestly as a practical synthesis inspired by PMI/Brightline/BRM and never claim official PMI status
source_heading: Cover; PMI/Brightline connection; PMI / Brightline foundations
input_fields: Provenance statement (verbatim B0004);Source (PMI Organizational Transformation Series; Brightline Initiative / Transformation Compass; PMI Benefits Realization Management);Used for
procedure: System displays the verbatim provenance statement in the Playbook reader, About page and generated report footers; the source-foundations table (Source / Used for) is shown read-only in the Playbook reader
permissions: edit-text:ADM(methodology admin, via versioned publish); view:all signed-in users
screen_api: Playbook and Procedures > About this methodology; GET /api/v1/methodology/provenance
acceptance: A01: provenance text on reader/About/report footer matches B0004 verbatim; an automated text scan of UI strings (en+ar) and report templates finds no claim of 'official PMI standard', 'PMI certified' or equivalent
notes: Playbook (B0004, B0024, B0155, B0156): the provenance statement and the source-foundations table (Source / Used for). Master-prompt additions (§2): showing the statement in the reader, the About page and report footers, and the automated scan for claims of official PMI status or certification. Interpretations: none beyond where the statement is displayed. The Arabic rendering of the statement needs linguistic review.

title: Mark custom extensions of the playbook distinctly from PMI/Brightline-derived foundations
source_heading: Source Base & What Is Custom; Custom extensions in this playbook
input_fields: Custom extension items: 6-phase integrated methodology;10-dimension Target Operating Model;stage-gate structure and most practical templates;initiative scoring model;governance cadence;30-60-90 launch plan;health check;worked roaming example;traceability chain
procedure: Each seeded methodology element (phases, TOM dimensions, gates, templates, scoring model, cadence, launch plan, health check, roaming example, traceability chain) carries a provenance attribute 'custom extension (playbook v1.0)' shown as a badge in the Playbook reader and Studio
permissions: edit:ADM(versioned publish only); view:all signed-in users
screen_api: Playbook and Procedures (element badges); Administration > Playbook Studio; GET /api/v1/methodology/elements?provenance=
acceptance: A01: every seeded element listed in B0158-B0162 returns provenance=custom-extension from the API and renders the badge in en and ar; no such element is labelled as a PMI standard
notes: Playbook (B0154, B0157-B0162): the list of custom extensions. Master-prompt additions: none; §2 M0089 restates the practical-synthesis distinction, and the provenance badge is how the platform displays the source list. Interpretations: B0160 says 'most practical templates', so the platform tags all of T01-T16 as custom extensions unless an admin records otherwise.

title: Offer the two source usage modes End-to-End and Modular when creating or entering a transformation
source_heading: How to use this playbook; One System, Two Modes
input_fields: Mode (choice: End-to-End | Modular);When to use;How;Entry phase (Modular only)
procedure: User creating a transformation selects a mode; the form shows the source 'When to use' and 'How' guidance for each mode; Modular requires an entry phase
output: Transformation record with mode and entry phase
permissions: create:TL,TO; edit-mode:TL,TO(before G1 approval; later via change request); view:scoped
automation: Transformation created -> instantiate phase checklist for the selected mode
acceptance: A01;A03: API accepts mode End-to-End or Modular only; Modular without entry phase is rejected with a validation error; guidance text shows 'Run Phases 1-6 sequentially...' and 'Enter at the relevant phase...' verbatim
notes: Playbook (B0007-B0009): the two modes with their 'When to use' and 'How' text, preserved verbatim. Master-prompt additions (§3 M0095; §4 M0125): Modular enters an existing transformation at a selected phase, so a Modular transformation records its entry phase; a material change to an approved scope goes through an impact assessment and reapproval. Interpretations: a change of mode after G1 approval is treated as such a material change (the listed material changes do not name the mode), so it needs a change request. (AN-08, finding F-DG0-006: provenance labels re-checked against source_ref.)

title: Enforce End-to-End sequencing: no initiative launch before North Star, outcomes and target state are clear
input_fields: Mode;G2 Direction approval state;G3 Target State approval state;Initiative launch request
procedure: Drafting is allowed at any time; the initiative launch/execution transition is blocked in End-to-End mode until G2 (North Star, outcomes) and G3 (target state) are approved or an authorized waiver is recorded
permissions: launch-initiative:TL after G2+G3 approved; waiver:SP (recorded, never automatic); view:scoped
automation: Gate approved -> enable next phase actions
screen_api: Initiatives and Roadmaps > Initiative > Launch; POST /api/v1/initiatives/{id}/launch
acceptance: A02;A08: in an End-to-End transformation with G3 not approved, POST launch returns 409 with reason 'North Star, outcomes and target state not yet approved'; after G2 and G3 approval the same call succeeds
notes: Playbook (B0009): 'Do not launch initiatives before the North Star, outcomes and target state are clear.' Master-prompt additions (§3 M0094, §4 M0125): drafts are allowed at any time, and an authorized waiver can stand in for a gate. Interpretations: 'launch' is the transition that authorizes execution, and 'clear' means G2 and G3 are approved.

title: Support Modular entry at a chosen phase or as a standalone TOM, business case or benefits register and flag missing links to outcomes and benefits
input_fields: Entry phase;Standalone deliverable type (Target Operating Model | initiative business case | benefits register);Inherited evidence;Minimum mandatory templates;Links to outcomes;Links to benefits
procedure: User enters at the relevant phase, completes the minimum mandatory templates, and reconnects to outcomes and benefits; the system lists missing upstream links and never marks earlier gates approved without recorded evidence
output: Modular transformation or standalone deliverable with missing-link report
automation: Missing mandatory evidence -> display missing items and block gate submission
acceptance: A03: a transformation entering at Design with no baseline and no outcome links shows both as missing and G3 submission is rejected by the API until they are supplied or an authorized waiver exists
notes: Playbook (B0008, B0009): Modular entry at the relevant phase; the standalone deliverables (TOM, initiative business case, benefits register); completing the minimum mandatory templates and reconnecting to outcomes and benefits. Master-prompt additions (§3 M0095): the missing-link report, and earlier gates are never marked approved without recorded evidence. Interpretations: the minimum mandatory templates per phase are configurable, with defaults set in Playbook Studio.

title: Apply 'Outcome before activity': initiatives cannot be submitted for prioritization without a linked measurable outcome
procedure: When an initiative is submitted to the prioritization scorecard or to G4 evidence, the system checks for at least one linked outcome with a KPI
screen_api: Initiatives and Roadmaps > Initiative > Submit; POST /api/v1/initiatives/{id}/submit
acceptance: A01: submitting an initiative with no outcome/KPI link returns a validation error naming 'Outcome before activity'; the same initiative with a link is accepted
notes: Playbook (B0011): the principle 'Outcome before activity'. Master-prompt additions: none. Interpretations: enforcing it as a validation when an initiative is submitted to prioritization or to G4; the source states the principle, not the checkpoint. (AN-08, finding F-DG0-006: provenance labels re-checked against source_ref.)

title: Apply 'Current state before solution': require a diagnostic covering economics, customer, operations, capability and technology before initiatives are prescribed
procedure: In End-to-End mode, initiatives created before the G1 diagnostic is approved stay in Draft; the diagnostic readiness shows which of the diagnosed areas are missing
output: Readiness indicator and draft-only initiative status
acceptance: A01;A02: before G1 approval an initiative cannot leave Draft (API 409); readiness lists missing diagnostic dimensions
notes: Playbook (B0012): the principle 'Current state before solution' and its five diagnosed areas. Master-prompt additions (§3 M0094): drafts may be prepared at any time, but required gate approvals are enforced before authorized execution. Interpretations: initiatives stay in Draft until G1 is approved, and the readiness indicator lists the diagnosed areas still missing. (AN-08, finding F-DG0-006: provenance labels re-checked against source_ref.)

title: Apply 'Operating model before execution': decision rights, ownership and cross-functional ways of working are explicit before execution
input_fields: Charter decision rights;T11 Decision Rights Matrix;T12 RACI;Owners
procedure: Execution-phase readiness (Transform) checks that the charter's decision rights are filled, T11 has at least the seeded decisions with an Approve role, and T12 has an accountable role per deliverable
acceptance: A01: readiness for Transform shows 'not ready' when T11 or charter decision rights are empty and 'ready' once they are completed
notes: Playbook (B0013): the principle 'Operating model before execution'. Master-prompt additions: none. Interpretations: the specific Transform readiness checks (charter decision rights filled, T11 seeded decisions with an Approve role, T12 one accountable role per deliverable); the source states the principle only. (AN-08, finding F-DG0-006: provenance labels re-checked against source_ref.)

title: Apply 'Benefits before closure': an initiative is complete only when value is realized and sustained, not when delivered
procedure: Initiatives carry separate delivery, value-realization and sustainment statuses; closure requires validated benefits and sustainment owner or a documented transition decision
output: Separate statuses; closure only when value conditions met
screen_api: Initiatives and Roadmaps > Initiative > Status; PATCH /api/v1/initiatives/{id}/status
acceptance: A11: an initiative with delivery=Complete and no validated benefit cannot be closed (API 409); UI shows 'Delivered — value validation pending'
notes: Playbook (B0014): the principle 'Benefits before closure'. Master-prompt additions (§3 M0092, §11 M0218): separate delivery, value-realization and sustainment statuses, and the documented transition decision. Interpretations: the closure rule (validated benefits plus a sustainment owner, or a transition decision), enforced as API 409.

title: Apply 'One source of truth': keep the charter, roadmap, initiative portfolio and benefits register linked as canonical records
procedure: Charter, roadmap, portfolio and benefits register reference the same canonical records (no copies); editing an initiative updates its roadmap and benefits views
acceptance: A01: renaming an initiative changes it in roadmap, scorecard and benefits register views in one update; no duplicate initiative rows exist in the database
notes: Playbook (B0015): keep the charter, roadmap, initiative portfolio and benefits register linked. Master-prompt additions (§5 M0150): the records are canonical and referenced, not copied. Interpretations: none.

title: Show the four guiding questions and tag each deliverable with the question it answers
input_fields: Question (Why change? | What must become different? | How will we execute? | How will we prove value?);Deliverable type
procedure: Each methodology template/deliverable carries one of the four questions, shown in form headers and the Playbook reader
screen_api: Playbook and Procedures; Administration > Playbook Studio > Templates
acceptance: A01: all four questions render verbatim (en) with ar translations; every seeded template has exactly one question tag
notes: Playbook (B0016): the four guiding questions. Master-prompt additions: none. Interpretations: mapping each template to exactly one question; the source gives the rule, not the mapping, so the seeded mapping is an analyst default. (AN-08, finding F-DG0-006: provenance labels re-checked against source_ref.)

title: Seed the six minimum governance roles with their source accountabilities and assign them per transformation
input_fields: Role (Executive Sponsor | Transformation Lead | Business Owners | Workstream Leads | Finance / Value Office | Transformation Office);Accountability;Assigned person or governed group;Scope
procedure: Admin seeds roles; Transformation Lead/Office assign named people to roles per transformation; accountability text shown on the role assignment
output: Role catalogue and per-transformation role assignments
permissions: assign:TO,TL; manage-catalogue:ADM; view:scoped; note:ADM cannot grant business approvals
screen_api: Administration > Organization and access; Transformation > Team; /api/v1/transformations/{id}/role-assignments
acceptance: A12: a user assigned Workstream Lead on transformation X cannot read transformation Y; role accountability text matches B0018
notes: Playbook (B0017, B0018): the six minimum governance roles and their accountability text. Master-prompt additions (§10 M0187): the implementation roles KDS, TD, CM/SEC, AUD and ADM; per-transformation scoped assignment; ADM cannot grant business approvals. Interpretations: none.

title: Restrict Finance / Value Office validation of baseline, benefit logic and value realization to the Finance role
source_heading: Minimum governance roles; Transformation Business Case
input_fields: Baseline validation status;Benefit logic validation status;Realized value validation status;Validator;Validation date
procedure: Only users holding FIN on the transformation can mark a baseline, benefit formula or realized value as validated; others can submit for validation
automation: Benefit evidence submitted -> route to Finance validation queue
screen_api: Benefits and Finance > Validation queue; POST /api/v1/validations
acceptance: A10;A12: a Business Owner calling the validate endpoint receives 403; a Finance user succeeds and the audit event records validator identity
notes: Playbook (B0018, B0084): Finance / Value Office validates the baseline, benefit logic and value realization, early and not after delivery. Master-prompt additions (§8 M0174; §10 M0188, M0211; §12 M0234; §16 M0330): validation is exclusive to FIN and enforced on the server (403 for anyone else), routed through a validation queue, and audited with the validator's identity. Interpretations: none.

title: Model the six phases with name, purpose, key outputs and phase objective
input_fields: Phase number;Phase name (DIAGNOSE | DEFINE | DESIGN | MOBILIZE | TRANSFORM | REALIZE);Purpose (Establish fact base | Set direction | Create target state | Build execution portfolio | Execute & govern | Prove & sustain value);Key outputs;Objective
procedure: Each transformation shows its current phase, the phase purpose, source objective text and key outputs with completion status
automation: Gate approved -> enable next phase and create its tasks
acceptance: A01;A02: API returns exactly six phases in order with names and purposes matching B0021; each phase page shows its objective text
notes: Playbook (B0020, B0021, B0027, B0046, B0054, B0068, B0091, B0119): the six phases with name, purpose, key outputs and objective. Master-prompt additions (§4 M0116): a phase advances only through gate approval, and the next phase's tasks are created. Interpretations: none.

title: Model the six stage gates G1-G6 as explicit approval records with decision question and evidence required
input_fields: Gate (G1 - Case for Change | G2 - Direction | G3 - Target State | G4 - Mobilization | G5 - Scale | G6 - Sustain);Decision question;Evidence required;Submission;Approver;Decision;Rationale
procedure: Owner assembles evidence, submits the gate; approver records decision against the evidence snapshot; gates are never inferred from task completion
output: Gate approval record tied to evidence snapshot
permissions: submit:TL; approve:SP (or configured approver); view:scoped; ADM cannot approve
automation: Valid gate submission -> route evidence snapshot to approvers
acceptance: A08: submission with missing mandatory evidence is rejected; approval by a non-approver returns 403; approval of a stale submission version is rejected
notes: Playbook (B0022, B0023, B0160): six gates with a decision question and the evidence required. The source names no gate approver. Master-prompt additions (§4 M0116, M0124; §10 M0213): explicit approval records tied to an evidence snapshot and never inferred from task completion; approval by a non-approver, or of a stale version, is rejected; ADM cannot approve. Interpretations: the default approver is the Executive Sponsor (B0018 'approves major trade-offs'), configurable per gate. Where T11 (B0099) names the decision a gate embodies, the gate can be configured to that approver: G3 per 'Target-state design' and G5 per 'Go-live / scale' (REQ-PB-018, REQ-PB-020). Gate workflow states and waivers are USER rows (REQ-S04-010, REQ-S04-013).

title: G1 Case for Change: require diagnostic, baseline, root causes and value pools as gate evidence
procedure: G1 checklist auto-links T01, baseline records and value pools; missing items block submission
automation: Mandatory gate evidence missing -> block submission
acceptance: A08: G1 submission without any value pool record returns a validation error listing 'Value pools'
notes: Playbook (B0023): the G1 evidence (diagnostic, baseline, root causes, value pools). Master-prompt additions (§4 M0125, §12 M0228): submission is blocked while mandatory evidence is missing. Interpretations: the checklist links T01, baseline records and value-pool records as the evidence items.

title: G2 Direction: require North Star, outcome tree, KPI definitions and guardrails as gate evidence
procedure: G2 checklist links North Star, T02 tree, KPI definitions and guardrails; missing items block submission
automation: Mandatory gate evidence missing -> block submission
acceptance: A08: G2 submission without guardrails is rejected listing 'Guardrails'
notes: Playbook (B0023): the G2 evidence (North Star, outcome tree, KPI definitions, guardrails). Master-prompt additions (§4 M0125): submission is blocked while mandatory evidence is missing. Interpretations: none.

title: G3 Target State: require Target Operating Model, capability gaps and future journeys as gate evidence
procedure: G3 checklist links TOM canvas/T03, capability gaps and future journeys; missing items block submission
permissions: submit:TL; approve:SP or BO per T11 'Target-state design'; view:scoped
automation: Mandatory gate evidence missing -> block submission
acceptance: A08: G3 submission with no future journey record is rejected listing 'Future journeys'
notes: Playbook (B0023): the G3 evidence (Target Operating Model, capability gaps, future journeys). Master-prompt additions (§4 M0125): submission is blocked while mandatory evidence is missing. Interpretations: the approver. B0023 names no gate approver; the default is SP, configurable to BO per T11 'Target-state design' (B0099).

title: G4 Mobilization: require initiative cards, business cases, roadmap, owners and capacity as gate evidence
procedure: G4 checklist links T05 cards, business cases, T07 roadmap, owners and capacity records; missing items block submission
automation: Mandatory gate evidence missing -> block submission
acceptance: A08: G4 submission where an initiative has no owner is rejected listing 'Owners'
notes: Playbook (B0023): the G4 evidence (initiative cards, business cases, roadmap, owners, capacity). Master-prompt additions (§4 M0125): submission is blocked while mandatory evidence is missing. Interpretations: none.

title: G5 Scale: require performance evidence, adoption, risk closure and decision log as gate evidence
procedure: G5 checklist links pilot/performance evidence, adoption indicators, closed or dispositioned risks and T16 entries
permissions: submit:TL; approve:SP (default) or BO per T11 'Go-live / scale' (configurable per gate); view:scoped
automation: Mandatory gate evidence missing -> block submission
acceptance: A08;A11: G5 submission with an open High-impact risk and no disposition is rejected listing 'Risk closure'; with the G5 approver configured to BO per T11 'Go-live / scale', an SP approval returns 403 and a BO approval succeeds
notes: Playbook (B0023): the G5 evidence (performance evidence, adoption, risk closure, decision log). Master-prompt additions (§4 M0122, M0125): 'risk closure' is met by closed risks or approved dispositions, and submission is blocked while mandatory evidence is missing. Interpretations: (1) The approver. B0023 names no gate approver. The default is SP (B0018 'approves major trade-offs'); it can be configured to BO per T11 'Go-live / scale' (B0099), in the same way as G3 in REQ-PB-018 (AN-05, finding F-DG0-002). G5 is the transformation-level gate. T11 'Go-live / scale' decisions on individual initiatives are separate decision records (Recommend: initiative owner; Approve: BO; Consult: Risk/Tech/CX; Inform: SteerCo) that feed G5's decision-log evidence. (2) 'High-impact' as the materiality threshold in the acceptance.

title: G6 Sustain: require benefits evidence, ownership transfer, controls and continuous improvement backlog as gate evidence
procedure: G6 checklist links validated benefit evidence, accepted BAU handover, controls and the CI backlog
automation: Mandatory gate evidence missing -> block submission
acceptance: A08;A11: G6 submission without an accepted BAU handover is rejected listing 'Ownership transfer'
notes: Playbook (B0023): the G6 evidence (benefits evidence, ownership transfer, controls, continuous-improvement backlog). Master-prompt additions (§4 M0125, §21 M0412): submission is blocked while mandatory evidence is missing, and product G6 never implies engineering gate DG7. Interpretations: none.

title: Enforce the Gate 1 rule: no list of projects proceeds until leadership agrees on problem, baseline and material value pools
input_fields: Leadership agreement on problem;Leadership agreement on baseline;Material value pools
procedure: G1 approval records explicit leadership agreement on problem, baseline and material value pools; before G1 approval (End-to-End) initiatives stay Draft and cannot enter the portfolio
acceptance: A08;A02: G1 approval without the three agreement confirmations is rejected; pre-G1, adding an initiative to the portfolio returns 409
notes: Playbook (B0032): do not proceed with a list of projects until the leadership team agrees on the problem, baseline and material value pools. Master-prompt additions: none. Interpretations: the agreement is recorded as three confirmations on the G1 decision, and before G1 (End-to-End) initiatives stay Draft and cannot enter the portfolio.

title: Organize the diagnostic into the six source workstreams with key questions and typical outputs
input_fields: Workstream (Business & Financial | Customer | Process & Operations | Organization & Governance | Technology & Data | Capability);Key questions;Typical outputs
procedure: Diagnose workspace lists the six workstreams with their key questions; users attach outputs (e.g. Baseline P&L bridge, value pools, trend analysis; journey pain points; process map; RACI gaps; architecture pain points; capability heatmap) as linked records or evidence
output: Diagnostic workstream records with linked outputs
acceptance: A01: the six workstreams and their key questions are seeded verbatim; an output linked to a workstream is persisted and shown in the G1 pack
notes: Playbook (B0029): the six workstreams with their key questions and typical outputs, seeded verbatim. Master-prompt additions: none. Interpretations: outputs are attached as linked records or evidence and shown in the G1 pack.

title: Provide an editable capability heatmap with build/buy/partner needs
source_heading: Core work (Capability); The 6-Phase Transformation System (Design: capabilities)
procedure: Users rate capabilities current vs target and record build/buy/partner need; gaps link to T03 and initiatives
acceptance: A01: a capability with a gap can be linked to a TOM gap row; heatmap renders from persisted ratings in en and ar
notes: Playbook (B0029, B0021): the capability heatmap with build/buy/partner needs. Master-prompt additions (§5 M0147): an owner, and links from capability gaps to T03 and to initiatives. Interpretations: the current/target rating scale, which the source does not give.

title: Provide journey and process maps capturing pain points, cycle time and failure demand
source_heading: Core work (Customer; Process & Operations); TOM dimension 3
input_fields: Journey/process name;Steps;Actors;Handoffs;Systems;Controls;Pain points;Cycle time;Failure demand;Current or future state
procedure: Users build current and future journey/process maps; future journeys serve as G3 evidence
screen_api: Target Operating Model > Journeys and processes; /api/v1/journeys
acceptance: A01: a future-state journey is linkable as G3 evidence; pain points link to T01 rows
notes: Playbook (B0029, B0021, B0056, B0023): journeys and processes with pain points, cycle time and failure demand; future journeys are G3 evidence. Master-prompt additions (§5 M0147): the steps, actors, handoffs, systems and controls fields. Interpretations: pain points link to T01 rows.

title: Implement Template 1 Current-State Diagnostic as a native register
procedure: Register pre-seeded with dimensions Financial, Customer, Process, People / Org, Technology, Data; users fill each row; Confidence is H / M / L; Impact accepts SAR or KPI
acceptance: A01: T01 form persists all 6 source columns; the six dimensions are pre-seeded; Confidence outside H/M/L is rejected by the API
notes: Playbook (B0030, B0031): T01's six columns, the six seeded dimensions, Confidence H / M / L and Impact as SAR or KPI. Master-prompt additions (§2 M0090): server-side validation, which rejects Confidence values outside H/M/L. Interpretations: none.

title: Record measurable baselines with metric, source and baseline date
source_heading: Template 1 (Evidence / baseline); Charter (Baseline date); Scope sanity check; Business case (Baseline)
input_fields: Baseline metric;Value;Unit;Source;Baseline date;Scope (Revenue | cost | customer | operational | capability);Validation status
procedure: Users record baselines referenced by T01, T02, T09, T14 and the business case; Finance validates; unvalidated baselines are labelled
acceptance: A01;A05: a baseline without a value or source is flagged 'not measurable'; a missing baseline shows Unknown, never zero
notes: Playbook (B0023, B0031, B0035, B0042, B0085): measurable baselines with metric and source, and a baseline date. Master-prompt additions (§5 M0149, §7 M0159, §8 M0174): a separate baseline registry (extension), a Finance validation status, and Unknown (never zero) when a baseline is missing. Interpretations: none.

title: Record value pools quantified by driver with upside and downside
procedure: Users quantify value pools by driver; material pools are flagged for G1 agreement; unquantified pools are labelled explicitly
acceptance: A01: a value pool without quantification is shown as 'unquantified', not zero; material pools appear in the G1 pack
notes: Playbook (B0021, B0023, B0029, B0032, B0085): value pools quantified by driver with upside and downside; material pools are G1 evidence. Master-prompt additions (§5 M0149, §4 M0118): the value-pool register (extension), and 'unquantified' labelling instead of zero. Interpretations: none.

title: Implement the Transformation Charter as a first-class record with all 14 source fields
input_fields: Transformation name;Executive sponsor;Transformation lead;Case for change;North Star;In scope;Out of scope;Baseline date;Target horizon;Top 3-5 outcomes;Strategic guardrails;Governance forum;Decision rights;Success definition
procedure: TL drafts the charter from the transformation workspace, links outcomes and guardrails, versions it, and submits it with G1/G2 evidence
acceptance: A01: the charter form persists all 14 fields; Baseline date is a valid date; a saved change creates a new charter version with history retained
notes: Playbook (B0034, B0035): the 14 charter fields. Master-prompt additions (§5 M0127): versioning with retained history. Interpretations: none. The transformation name is created in P1 and the full charter in P2.

title: Capture the transformation thesis in its four-part causal sentence
input_fields: Capabilities / journeys / operating model changed;Customer/operational outcomes improved;Financial/strategic benefits created;Evidence / causal logic
procedure: Charter includes a structured thesis; the system renders 'If we change ..., then ... will improve, which will create ..., because ...'
acceptance: A01: thesis with any of the four parts empty is flagged incomplete; rendered sentence matches the source structure
notes: Playbook (B0036, B0037): the four-part thesis sentence. Master-prompt additions: none; §5 M0146 restates the thesis sentence. Interpretations: a thesis with any part empty is flagged incomplete.

title: Run the five scope sanity checks on the charter
input_fields: Is scope tied to outcomes rather than departments?;Can each major scope item be traced to a diagnosed problem or opportunity?;Are explicit exclusions documented?;Is the baseline measurable?;Are executive decisions required to unblock the transformation visible?;Response;Evidence
procedure: Charter shows the five checks; system pre-evaluates checks it can (exclusions present, baseline measurable, scope items linked to T01) and users confirm the rest with evidence
output: Scope sanity check result on the charter
acceptance: A01: all five questions render verbatim; an empty Out of scope field makes 'Are explicit exclusions documented?' fail
notes: Playbook (B0038-B0043): the five questions, verbatim. Master-prompt additions (§5 M0146): the five scope sanity checks are part of the native charter record. Interpretations: the response values (Yes/No/Partial), which neither source gives, and the system's pre-evaluation of the checks it can compute. (AN-08, finding F-DG0-006: provenance labels re-checked against source_ref.)

title: Model the outcome hierarchy from North Star to strategic outcomes, KPIs, targets and initiative contribution
input_fields: Level (North Star | Strategic Outcomes | KPIs | Targets | Initiative Contribution);Definition;Example
procedure: Users build a linked tree; initiatives link to outcomes with a contribution statement
acceptance: A01: tree nodes for all five levels persist and link; an initiative contribution without an outcome link is rejected
notes: Playbook (B0047, B0048): the five levels from North Star to initiative contribution. Master-prompt additions: none; §5 M0130 restates the hierarchy from North Star to initiative contributions. Interpretations: an initiative contribution without an outcome link is rejected.

title: Hold exactly one current North Star per transformation, stated as one concise sentence
procedure: The North Star is edited on the charter and shown at the top of the outcome tree and transformation header
acceptance: A01: creating a second active North Star for the same transformation returns 409; the transformation header shows the North Star
notes: Playbook (B0035, B0048): the North Star is one concise sentence describing the future outcome. Master-prompt additions: none. Interpretations: exactly one current North Star per transformation, so a second active one is rejected (409).

title: Implement Template 2 Outcome & KPI Tree as a native register
procedure: Users enter each outcome with its KPI, baseline, target, target date, owner and leading indicator; rows link into the outcome hierarchy
screen_api: Strategy and KPIs > Outcome & KPI tree; /api/v1/transformations/{id}/outcome-kpis
acceptance: A01: T02 persists all 7 source columns; a row without Target date is rejected (targets are time-bound per B0048)
notes: Playbook (B0049, B0050, B0048): T02's seven columns; targets are time-bound. Master-prompt additions: none; §5 M0130 restates T02's columns. Interpretations: Target date is mandatory (from 'time-bound' in B0048).

title: Warn when the charter does not hold 3-5 top outcomes
procedure: Charter counts linked top outcomes and shows a warning below 3 or above 5; G2 readiness shows the count
acceptance: A01: a charter with 2 top outcomes shows the warning; with 4 it does not
notes: Playbook (B0035): 'Top 3-5 outcomes'. Master-prompt additions: none. Interpretations: '3-5' is read as guidance, so a count outside it warns rather than blocks. (AN-08, finding F-DG0-006: provenance labels re-checked against source_ref.)

title: Apply the good outcome test to every outcome
input_fields: Specific;Measurable;Strategically relevant;Owned by a business leader;Achievable through a defined causal chain
procedure: Each outcome shows the five criteria; system checks measurable (KPI linked), owned (owner set) and flags statements that are only 'launch', 'implement' or 'deliver'
screen_api: Strategy and KPIs > Outcome > Quality check
acceptance: A01: an outcome worded 'Launch new app' with no KPI fails the test with reasons; G2 readiness lists failing outcomes
notes: Playbook (B0051): the five criteria and the 'not just launch, implement or deliver' wording. Master-prompt additions: none. Interpretations: the automated checks (KPI linked, owner set) and the keyword flagging; neither source specifies how the test is evaluated. title: Implement the Target Operating Model Canvas with the ten source boxes and prompts

The agenda, per-dimension contribution capture, conversion into actions and the no-close-with-unconverted-items rule are master prompt §5 additions (M0147), not playbook content; the 90-120-minute workshop with business owners and conversion into design decisions with owners is source (B0063).

title: Implement Template 4 Design Decision Log as a native register

notes: Playbook (B0064, B0065): T04's seven columns, IDs D-01, D-02…, Options A / B / C and Status Open. Master-prompt additions (§5 M0150): one decision model shared with T16. Interpretations: none.

title: Maintain the traceability chain from diagnosed issue to benefit with a view and orphan report

title: Implement Template 5 Initiative Card as a native record

acceptance: A01: T05 persists all 14 source fields; Key deliverables outside 3-7 shows a warning
notes: Playbook (B0071, B0072): the 14 initiative-card fields; BO is accountable (A) for Initiative Delivery in T12 (B0101). Master-prompt additions: none; §5 M0133 restates the card fields. Interpretations: '3-7 deliverables' is a guidance range, so it warns rather than blocks.

title: Require every initiative to be traced to a target-state gap and an outcome
source_heading: Initiative Card (Problem / gap addressed; Outcome/KPI contribution)
procedure: Submission of an initiative for G4 requires at least one TOM/diagnostic gap link and one outcome/KPI link
acceptance: A01;A08: G4 submission containing an initiative with no gap link is rejected naming that initiative
notes: Playbook (B0072, B0070): every initiative references a diagnostic/TOM gap and an outcome/KPI contribution. Master-prompt additions (§4 M0125): the rule is enforced as mandatory G4 evidence. Interpretations: the check runs when G4 is submitted.

title: Implement Template 6 Prioritization Scorecard as a native register
procedure: Scorers enter 1-5 per criterion for each initiative; Weighted score is calculated; ranked table shown
acceptance: A01: T06 persists all criteria per initiative; Weighted score is read-only (calculated)
notes: Playbook (B0074-B0076): T06's criteria, weights and calculated weighted score. Master-prompt additions: none; §5 M0134 restates T06's criteria, weights and weighted result. Interpretations: which roles may score (for example, FIN scores financial value).

title: Apply T06 default weights 25/25/20/15/15 with a 1-5 scale and a calculated weighted score
input_fields: Strategic fit weight 25%;Financial value weight 25%;Customer impact weight 20%;Feasibility weight 15%;Time-to-value weight 15%;Score 1-5
procedure: Weighted score = sum(score x weight) on the 1-5 scale; scores outside 1-5 rejected; missing score marks the row incomplete
acceptance: A01;A05: scores 5,4,3,2,1 give 3.30 (decimal, exact); a score of 6 is rejected; a missing score shows 'incomplete', not a numeric total
notes: Playbook (B0076): the weights 25/25/20/15/15, the 1-5 scale and a calculated weighted score. Master-prompt additions (§9 M0176): weighted score = sum(score × weight), giving a 1-5 result, and a missing score means incomplete, not zero. Interpretations: none.

title: Adjust T06 weights per transformation, including risk/compliance replacing part of the weighting, with a 100% total check and versioned weight sets
procedure: Authorized users propose an adjusted weight set for a transformation, optionally with a risk/compliance criterion that replaces part of the weighting; the server rejects any set whose weights do not total 100%; an approved set becomes a new immutable version, earlier versions are kept, and every scoring and ranking records the weight-set version it used
automation: Weight set approved -> rescore and record the version as the cause of rank changes
screen_api: Initiatives and Roadmaps > Prioritization > Weights; PUT /api/v1/transformations/{id}/prioritization/weight-sets
acceptance: A01;A05;A07: saving weights totalling 95% (or 105%) is rejected with a validation error; a risk/compliance criterion at 10% with strategic fit reduced to 15% is accepted as weight-set version 2 and rescoring uses it; scores computed under version 1 keep their version-1 reference; the REQ-S09-005 ranking history can name 'weight version 2' as the cause of a rank change
notes: Playbook (B0077): adjust weights to the transformation context; for regulated or safety-critical transformations, risk/compliance can replace part of the weighting. Master-prompt additions (§9 M0176): weights must total 100%, and approved weights are versioned. Interpretations: weight sets are per transformation and approved by SP. AN-05 split (finding F-DG0-001): this row keeps the per-transformation adjustment, the 100% check and weight-set versioning. The DG3 evidence 'invalid weights … handled' (M0406) and REQ-S09-005 (DG3) need these, so the row completes at DG3 (was P3;P5/DG5). Administrator-configured defaults and rubrics in Playbook Studio are now REQ-PB-093 (DG5). AN-04 consolidation: absorbs former REQ-S09-002 (Make scoring rubrics and approved weights configurable and versioned); its anchor M0176 is carried here, and its Studio part moved to REQ-PB-093.

title: Implement Template 7 Wave Roadmap with the four seeded source waves
procedure: Seed Wave 0 — Mobilize (0-6 weeks), Wave 1 — Prove (1-3 months), Wave 2 — Scale (3-9 months), Wave 3 — Embed (6-18 months) with source purpose, entry criteria and exit evidence; initiatives are assigned to waves with dates
acceptance: A01: four waves seeded with values verbatim (e.g. '0-6 weeks', 'Sponsor + charter'); overlapping horizons are accepted
notes: Playbook (B0078, B0079): the four waves with purpose, typical horizon, entry criteria and exit evidence, seeded verbatim. Master-prompt additions (§5 M0135; §9 M0178, M0180-M0183): T07 links initiatives, dates and milestones to each wave, and the four source waves (restated in M0180-M0183) are seeded as overlapping planning horizons, not rigid deadlines, which is why overlapping horizons are accepted. title: Implement Template 8 Dependency Map as a native register

acceptance: A01: T08 persists all 7 columns; From accepts an initiative or 'External'; a cycle A->B->A is reported
notes: Playbook (B0080, B0081): T08's seven columns, with From as an initiative or External. Master-prompt additions (§9 M0184, §12 M0232): cycle detection, and notifying owners when a critical dependency slips. Interpretations: the T08 record is the canonical record that RAID Dependency entries reference (see B0126, REQ-PB-078).

title: Support T08 dependency types Decision, Tech, Data and Vendor plus configurable types
procedure: Type is a choice seeded with Decision / Tech / Data / Vendor; admins may add types
acceptance: A01: the four source types are present and cannot be deleted; an unknown type value is rejected by the API
notes: Playbook (B0081): the types Decision / Tech / Data / Vendor. Master-prompt additions (§5 M0136): admins can add further (configurable) types. Interpretations: the four source types cannot be deleted.

title: Implement the Transformation Business Case with all ten source sections
procedure: TL drafts the case; Investment split into Capex, opex, internal FTE, vendor cost, opportunity cost; Benefits into revenue uplift, cost reduction, avoidance, working capital, strategic/non-financial; Timing records benefit ramp, one-off vs recurring and implementation horizon; Risks & sensitivities records key assumptions and downside/upside cases; Ownership names benefit owner, initiative owner and Finance validator; Decision ask names Funding / policy / resource / prioritization
permissions: create/edit:TL; co-author:FIN (R per RACI); approve:SP (A per RACI); view:scoped

notes: Playbook (B0083, B0085): the ten sections and their content. Master-prompt additions (§5 M0148, §16 M0329): exactly one classification per investment line, and SAR amounts stored as decimals. Interpretations: none.

title: Support a transformation-level business case with lighter linked initiative cases
procedure: Initiative cases are lighter forms linked to the transformation case; roll-up references, not copies

notes: Playbook (B0084): a transformation-level case, with lighter initiative cases underneath. Master-prompt additions (§8 M0173): the roll-up works by reference and never duplicates benefits. Interpretations: none.

title: Require Finance validation of baseline and benefit logic early, before G4, not after delivery

title: Implement Template 9 Benefit Formula as a native register
procedure: Users define each benefit's baseline driver, change assumption, formula, ramp (e.g. Q1-Q4) and Confidence H/M/L; formulas use a restricted expression language

title: Seed the two source benefit formula examples
input_fields: Revenue uplift (Customers x attach rate x ARPU; Attach +X pp; Δ attach x customers x ARPU; Q1-Q4; M);Cost reduction (Volume x unit cost; Unit cost -X%; Volume x Δ unit cost; Q2-Q3; H)

acceptance: A05: attach 0.10->0.12 with 100000 customers and ARPU 50 SAR yields 100000 SAR (decimal exact); cost example Volume x Δ unit cost computes exactly

Allocation limits: REQ-S08-013; overlap warnings: REQ-S08-014.

title: Record owners and capacity for mobilization

notes: Playbook (B0021, B0023, B0079): owners and capacity (Mobilize resourcing, G4 evidence, Wave 2 entry 'Evidence + capacity'). Master-prompt additions (§5 M0149, §9 M0177): the resource/capacity plan register (extension) and capacity-conflict indicators. Interpretations: none.

title: Seed the five transformation operating system layers with cadence, purpose, participants and outputs

notes: Playbook (B0092, B0093, B0161): the five layers with cadence, purpose, participants and outputs. Master-prompt additions (§10 M0196, §12 M0235): meetings generated on a configurable recurrence, and a draft agenda at the cut-off. Interpretations: none.

notes: Playbook (B0093): the outputs of each layer. Master-prompt additions (§10 M0212): outputs are native meeting records, and decisions recorded there flow into T16. (AN-08, finding F-DG0-006: provenance labels re-checked against source_ref.)

title: Implement Template 10 Executive Transformation Dashboard with its six source areas

notes: Playbook (B0094, B0095): the six areas and what each one shows. Master-prompt additions (§13 M0244): the dashboard renders from live canonical data, with drill-down to contributing records. Interpretations: none.

title: Show a Decisions area Red when an executive decision is overdue

notes: Playbook (B0095): 'Red if executive decision overdue'. Master-prompt additions (§10 M0196, §15 M0302): the rule is evaluated daily in the configured timezone (default Asia/Riyadh). Interpretations: none.

title: Implement Template 11 Decision Rights Matrix with the four seeded source rows

notes: Playbook (B0098, B0099): the four decisions with Recommend / Approve / Consult / Inform and SLA, seeded verbatim. Master-prompt additions (§12 M0231): approvals are routed per the matrix, and an expired SLA escalates. Interpretations: none.

input_fields: SLA type (working days | Next SteerCo / urgent route | Per release plan);Working days

notes: Playbook (B0099): the three SLA types (working days; Next SteerCo / urgent route; Per release plan). Master-prompt additions (§10 M0196): a configurable business calendar (default Asia/Riyadh) with workweek and holidays. Interpretations: how 'Next SteerCo / urgent route' and 'Per release plan' resolve to due dates.

title: Implement Template 12 RACI with the six seeded deliverables and R/A/C/I values including A/R

notes: Playbook (B0100, B0101): the six deliverables with their R/A/C/I values, including A/R. Master-prompt additions (§10 M0203, M0211): the source RACI is a configurable starting point, roles map to named people, and each deliverable has one accountable (REQ-S10-009). Interpretations: none.

title: Enforce the governance rule: escalate decisions, not status

notes: Playbook (B0102): 'Escalate decisions, not status'; every executive agenda item 'should' state the five elements. (AN-08, finding F-DG0-006: the publication block was mislabelled as an interpretation.)

title: Manage adoption as an outcome with measurable leading indicators, separate from delivery

notes: Source-grounded core (cited B blocks). AN-04 consolidation: absorbs former REQ-S11-003 (Track adoption actuals against adoption trajectories and create corrective interventions when gaps appear); its anchors M0216 and acceptance are carried here. Trajectory-based adoption tracking and the exactly-one-intervention rule are master prompt §11 additions (M0216); adoption as an outcome with leading indicators, separate from delivery, is source (B0105). Indicators: REQ-PB-071/072.

title: Implement Template 13 Stakeholder & Adoption Plan as a native register
procedure: Users record each stakeholder group; Impact H/M/L; Current stance Support / Neutral / Resist; Intervention Comms / training / involvement / incentive

notes: Playbook (B0106, B0107): T13's seven columns and the value lists (H/M/L; Support / Neutral / Resist; Comms / training / involvement / incentive). notes: Playbook (B0108-B0115): the seven leading adoption indicators. Master-prompt additions (§11 M0216): the indicators are KPI templates with actuals by period, and an actual below trajectory creates an intervention. Interpretations: none.

notes: Playbook (B0116): involve impacted teams early in design; champions surface constraints and shape decisions. Master-prompt additions: none. notes: Playbook (B0122, B0123): T14's ten columns, IDs B01, B02… and Status R/A/G. Master-prompt additions (§8 M0166, M0174): realized value awaiting Finance validation is labelled pending and excluded from validated totals. Interpretations: none.

title: Enforce scoped write access: implementers are limited to their scope, each reviewer writes only its own review records and evidence, QA may add tests, and gate rules, agent definitions and sources are protected
source_heading: §0.1 Verify capabilities and establish the workspace
procedure: Two layers enforce tools/agents/write-scopes.json. (1) File tools: a PreToolUse hook (guard-write.mjs) in every run's settings blocks Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit outside the role's scope; it takes its root from MTH_GUARD_ROOT and fails closed without it, guards the repository and every worktree, checks both the lexical and the symlink-resolved path, matches deny rules case-insensitively, fails closed when the worktree list cannot be read, fails closed on a path whose real path cannot be determined or whose resolution passes through /proc, /sys or /dev (for example a symlink to /proc/<pid>/root) (F-DG0-143), and treats only the run's own private temporary directory (MTH_RUN_TMP; without the runner, the OS temp directory) as scratch, never the shared /tmp and never home (D-009, D-020, D-023, D-024, D-028). Each reviewer's file-tool scope is only its own review files (docs/delivery/reviews/*/round-*/<role>.*) and its own evidence directory (docs/delivery/test-evidence/*/<key>/**, key domain, code-security, qa or audit), so concurrently running reviewers cannot write each other's records, sidecars or evidence (F-DG0-144, D-028). (2) Shell: run-agent.sh generates each run's settings with tools/agents/agent_settings.py, adding a Claude Code Bash sandbox (bubblewrap; enabled, failIfUnavailable, allowUnsandboxedCommands false) whose denyWrite list covers .git, .claude, .mcp.json, CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, .gitignore, .gitattributes, .github, tools/gates, tools/agents, tools/source, docs/source, trading_agent and the delivery records (reviews, gates, runs, candidates, assignments, findings.json, stages.json) in the repository and every worktree; for reviewers and the transformation-analyst it also denies every existing path outside the role's own areas; agent_settings.py takes the run's stage, confines each reviewer's shell to its own evidence directory docs/delivery/test-evidence/<stage>/<key> and explicitly denies the other reviewers' evidence directories even before they exist, while the transformation-analyst and implementers may write no evidence (docs/delivery/test-evidence is denied) (D-028); the only writable scratch is the run's private TMPDIR, since the sandbox allows $TMPDIR/claude-0 and leaves /tmp and /var/tmp read-only (D-028); agents start with --setting-sources project, so user or local settings cannot switch the hook off (D-025). The validator accepts a gate's review and audit records only from runs whose recorded settings (settings.json, matching meta.settings_sha256) enforce that sandbox and whose deny list names .git, .claude, tools/gates, tools/agents, docs/source, docs/delivery/reviews and docs/delivery/runs under the run's own working directory, meta.cwd (D-025, F-DG0-230). The runner's before-and-after configuration scan covers user Claude settings, git config and excludes, hooks including symlinks, and Claude configuration and ignore files anywhere in the repository and worktrees, ignored by git or not; it skips zero-length, untracked, non-symlink files (the sandbox's own stubs), reports added, changed and removed entries (a removed entry as '<path> removed', so a configuration file that is deleted or truncated to zero length, including an ignored file such as .claude/settings.local.json, is reported; snapshot entries are tab-separated so paths with spaces stay unambiguous) and fails closed (if the comparison itself fails, the run counts as changed), records changes as external_config_changed, refuses to auto-commit a reviewer or analyst run (exit 71) and warns for an implementer run (D-024, D-025, D-026, D-027)
output: Write guard, per-run Bash sandbox settings, scope table, validator sandbox binding, configuration scan and tests

title: Install dependencies only inside an OS sandbox: the orchestrator's install step runs under bubblewrap with network limited to the package registry, a read-only root filesystem, only the target tree and package store writable, lifecycle scripts disabled unless allow-listed, and a committed lockfile

procedure: Agent shells have no network (D-025), so dependency installation is an orchestrator step. The orchestrator never runs it with its own unconfined privileges: an installation wrapper (delivered and tested in P1 before the first install) runs the package manager inside bubblewrap with network allowed for the package registry, the root filesystem read-only, only the target tree (for example node_modules or the virtual environment) and the package store writable, package lifecycle scripts (install/postinstall and similar) disabled unless the package is on a reviewed allow-list, and a frozen install from the committed lockfile (the install fails if the lockfile is missing or would change); later build and test commands that execute installed package code also run only inside the sandbox (D-026, D-027, F-DG0-142)

screen_api: installation wrapper script and its tests (planned P1 names, fixed by the P1 ADRs); lockfile; lifecycle-script allow-list
acceptance: A18;A23;A24: the P1 wrapper tests show, under the wrapper, that (1) a write outside the target tree and package store fails with a read-only filesystem error; (2) a package lifecycle script not on the allow-list does not run, while an allow-listed one does; (3) an install without a committed lockfile, or one that would change the lockfile, fails non-zero; (4) a missing bubblewrap makes the wrapper exit non-zero (BLOCKED, never an unsandboxed install); and the first dependency install of P1 is shown in the run evidence to have gone through the wrapper
notes: implementation-assumption: the mechanism (bubblewrap, registry-only network, read-only root, writable target tree and package store, lifecycle scripts off unless allow-listed) is the orchestrator's implementation decision D-027 in response to F-DG0-142 (docs/delivery/threat-model.md residual 3), not master-prompt text. The source grounding is M0012 (do not weaken existing permission controls to enable the workflow: the agent sandbox of D-025 must not be bypassed by an unconfined install), M0314 (pin compatible versions and lockfiles), M0331 (dependency checks) and M0404 (P1 repo/build/CI). Classified P1/DG1 per the §21 stage table: the first dependency install happens in P1 (repo/build/CI, M0404), and DG0 installs none. Residual (threat model 3): the content of the installed packages themselves; package code executes only inside the sandbox. Related: REQ-S16-009 (pinning and licence inventory, DG7), REQ-S19-003 (handover manifests and lockfiles).
